cohort: The study included 217 term newborn infants delivered by cesarean section whose umbilical cord clamping times were recorded and who had cord blood samples.
finding: There was no significant relationship between early and late umbilical cord clamping and cord blood acid-base parameters or hemoglobin values in term newborns delivered by cesarean section.
mod_finding: The findings specifically apply to term newborns delivered by cesarean section, showing no significant difference in cord blood gas parameters or hemoglobin based on cord clamping time in this birth mode.
